title: Triage, Communications, and Restoration Blueprint
author: Leila Thompson
content:
Summary

This blueprint documents a standardized triage-to-restoration workflow, customer and status-page communication templates, example runbooks, and a game-day syllabus for validating on-call readiness. It is intended for SREs, service owners, and incident responders across Redwood Inference. The goal is consistent, fast, and auditable incident handling that minimizes customer impact while preserving data privacy and meeting SLAs.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood-hosted inference services and control plane endpoints (api.redwood.example, runtime.redwood.example, auth.redwood.example).
- Excludes vendor-managed external dependencies beyond core infra (see external-dependency-handling section).

Objectives

1. Reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) to <= 2 minutes for P0/P1 alerts.
2. Reduce mean time to restore (MTTR) for P0 incidents to <= 30 minutes for single-region failures.
3. Provide clear, templated customer communications within 30 minutes of incident detection for externally visible issues.
4. Ensure all incidents receive a documented postmortem within 72 hours of mitigation.

Roles & Responsibilities

- Pager (Primary on-call): Acknowledge alerts, perform initial triage, escalate according to severity matrix.
- Incident Commander (IC): Coordinates workstreams, points of contact for execs/CS, owns incident timeline.
- Subject Matter Expert (SME): Service owner or runtime engineer who implements fixes and runbook actions.
- Communications Lead (Comms): Publishes status updates, coordinates customer notifications with CS.
- Scribe: Records timeline, actions, and decisions in the incident page.

On-call Rotation Model

- Team: Core SRE + service-specific rotations (e.g., Serving Runtime, Control Plane, Networking).
- Cadence: 1-week primary, 2-week secondary.
- Handoff: Each rotation must complete the Handoff Checklist 15 minutes before the next shift. The checklist: 
  1) Confirm alert backlog cleared.
  2) Share outstanding actions and timelines.
  3) Verify monitoring dashboards loaded and API tokens accessible.
  4) Update the oncall-handover page.

Severity Matrix (quick reference)

| Severity | Customer Impact | Pager Action | Typical SLAs | Escalation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P0 (Critical) | Widespread outage or single-customer data loss | Immediate page, IC declared within 5 min | MTTA <= 2m, MTTR <= 30m | Escalate to engineering director and on-call SRE manager |
| P1 (High) | Significant degradation (e.g., 50% requests high latency) | Page primary, engage SME | MTTR target 2 hours | Notify product/CS for affected customers |
| P2 (Medium) | Partial degradation, workaround available | Alert to oncall (email/Slack) | MTTR target 1 business day | Triage during business hours |
| P3 (Low) | Informational, minor errors | Ticket in backlog | No SLA | Owner triages in regular sprint planning |

Triage Procedure (step-by-step)

1) Acknowledge: Pager acknowledges in the paging tool within MTTA target. Record ack time in incident page.
2) Quick assessment (first 5 minutes): 
   - Verify alert fidelity: noise vs. real degradation (run queries: `curl -s https://internal-monitoring/api/v1/query?query=error_rate{service=\"serving\"}`)
   - Collect core signals: request rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, GPU utilization, queue length, KV cache hit ratio.
3) Declare severity and assign IC if P0/P1.
4) Containment: apply safe, reversible mitigations (scale up, disable non-critical features, route to fallback model variant).
5) Restore: apply long-lived fix (configuration change, deployment rollback, hot-patch).
6) Communicate: publish initial status (templates below), update every 30 minutes for P0 until mitigation.
7) Post-incident: create postmortem, run RCA, schedule follow-up with owners and track action items to closure.

Example Commands & Diagnostics

- Check serving error rates: `kubectl -n serving exec -c exporter -it metrics-collector -- curl -s http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep request_errors`
- Inspect pods by restart count: `kubectl get pods -n runtime --sort-by=.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount`
- Query Prometheus p95 latency: `curl -s -G http://prometheus/api/v1/query --data-urlencode 'query=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{service=\"serving\"}[5m])) by (le))'`
- Increase replica set (temporary): `kubectl scale deploy serving-api --replicas=6 -n serving`

Runbook: High Inference Latency (serving.redwood.example)

Symptoms
- P95 latency > 2s and error rate > 3% for > 5 minutes.
- Autoscaler not increasing capacity, GPU queue length > 80% sustained.

Immediate Actions (IC/Primary)
1) Confirm metrics and correlate with recent deploys: check last deploy timestamp `deploy-tracker > serving-api`.
2) If autoscaler unhealthy, restart HPA controller: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/hpa-controller -n infra` and watch `kubectl get hpa -n serving`.
3) If queue backlog high, enable burst capacity: toggle runbook flag `feature-toggle burst-capacity serving-api` (UI path: Console > Runtime > Feature Flags).
4) If root cause is a model regression (increased per-token time), fallback to verified model variant: `POST /api/v1/models/route` with body `{ \"service\": \"serving\", \"model\": \"gptq-1.3-verified\" }` (see API examples in eng-developer-experience/docs).
5) If no quick fix, scale pods/gpus as short-term mitigation. Record any configuration changes in the incident log.

Safeguards
- All runbook changes that affect customers require a tested rollback plan and approval from IC.
- Avoid data-destructive actions unless approved by IC and Security.

Communications

Status Page Template (for public status.redwood.example)

- Title: [Investigating / Degraded / Major Outage] — Serving API (api.redwood.example)
- Incident ID: {INC-YYYYMMDD-####}
- Summary: Brief 1–2 lines describing user impact.
- Impacted Customers: All / Subset (list tags or org IDs).
- Current status: Investigation / Mitigated / Monitoring / Restored.
- Next update: {timestamp + 30m}
- Contact: support@redwood.example (for customers with SLA).

Customer Email Template (first outbound, 30-minute window)

Subject: Service interruption affecting inference (api.redwood.example) — {INC-...}

Hello {Customer Name},

We are investigating a service disruption impacting inference requests to api.redwood.example. Our on-call team is actively triaging. At this time:
- Impact: {describe impact: e.g., 20% requests failing or retries increasing} 
- Mitigation steps in progress: {e.g., failing model variant isolated, autoscale increased} 
- Next update: {time + 30 minutes}

We apologize for the disruption. If you need immediate assistance, open a support ticket or contact your CS lead.

Thank you,
Redwood Inference Operations

Slack/Chat Update Template (internal)

[INC-...][P0/P1] Serving latency spike — primary acknowledged. Current hypothesis: model regression. Steps: 1) fallback to verified model; 2) scale replicas; 3) monitor p95. IC: {Name}. Comms: {Name}. Scribe: {Name}.

Postmortem Expectations & Timeline

- Draft due: within 72 hours of mitigation. Must include timeline, RCA, contributing factors, action items, and owner for each action.
- Severity classification confirmed by leadership before closure.
- Postmortem review meeting: within 7 days of incident closure with engineering, product, and CS representation.

Postmortem Template (fields to populate)

- Title
- Incident ID
- Dates/times (detection, mitigation, restore, close)
- Summary (2–3 sentences)
- Impact (customers affected, SLO breaches)
- Timeline (minute-granular with source links)
- Root Cause(s)
- Contributing factors
- Corrective actions (short-term and long-term) with owners and due dates
- Follow-ups & verification steps

Game Day / Simulation Syllabus

Purpose: Validate the triage workflow, runbook accuracy, communications, and escalation.

Frequency: Quarterly for each product area; mini-sims monthly for new hires.

Basic 3-hour agenda:
- 00:00–00:15: Briefing & objectives
- 00:15–01:15: Inject 1 (latency/regression) — live triage and comms
- 01:15–01:30: Break and quick retrospective
- 01:30–02:15: Inject 2 (multi-region failover) — focus on routing and fallback policies
- 02:15–02:45: Post-exercise postmortem writeup (10–15 minute timeline)
- 02:45–03:00: Hotwash and action assignment

Scoring criteria:
- MTTA (ack within target)
- Accuracy of severity assignment
- Correct use of templates and cadence of customer updates
- Runbook adherence and rollback verification

Tools & Integrations

- PagerDuty: primary alerting and escalation. Alert runbooks must include runbook URL and owner.
- Slack: incident channel naming convention `#incident-{INC-ID}`; pinned incident page link.
- Status Page: status.redwood.example for public updates; internal-status for private updates to customers.
- Confluence: incident timeline and postmortem pages using template `incident-template-v2`.
- Monitoring: Prometheus, Grafana, and Synthetics (end-to-end checks every 15s for critical routes).

Audit & Compliance Notes

- All incident pages must include audit metadata: acknowledged_by, ack_time, actions_taken, and changelog entries for any infra changes.
- For incidents with customer data exposure, notify Security immediately and follow the data-exposure runbook (security-and-compliance/data-exposure).

Appendix: Quick Reference Checklists

Handoff Checklist (repeat)
- Clear outstanding alerts or assign owners.
- Confirm runbook access and API tokens.
- Share key dashboards and the last 24h incident digest.

Incident Close Checklist
- Postmortem draft created and reviewers assigned.
- All action items have owners and target dates.
- Incident page linked to status updates and customer emails.
- Incident marked with final severity and SLO breach status.
